pages.title: Terrain-Aware Streams
pages.text: River ends that would otherwise stop abruptly can form headwater streams. A stream seeks a natural downhill route and gradually joins an existing main river while retaining TFC river biomes, water, and related features.

pages.title: Flow and River Mouths
pages.text: The uppermost block remains a stable source. Later sections can form bends, rapids, waterfalls, and spreading flow.$(br2)Static river water uses 16 directions; near the main river, bed height, water level, width, and flow hand over gradually to avoid blockages or sudden cliffs.

pages.title: Underground Streams
pages.text: Deeper stream sections turn into underground streams. They tend to appear in higher-terrain biomes, showing up where the stream goes deep underground.

pages.title: Generation Scope
pages.text: Streams appear only in new worlds or previously ungenerated chunks. They avoid the full banks of unrelated main rivers and protect material around a wet bed without filling entire natural caves.
